summary_en: North Pacific Bank raised its full-year dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 2027 by 4.50 yen to 36.50 yen per share, reflecting upward revisions to net profit guidance. Interim dividends (Q2, Q3) were also increased by 1.50 yen each to 9.50 yen, with an expected payout ratio of approximately 40 percent.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Business Forecast and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
North Pacific Bank announced a revision to its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The annual dividend per share has been increased by 4.50 yen to 36.50 yen, compared to the previous forecast of 32.00 yen announced on May 13, 2026. This represents an increase of 8.50 yen compared to the previous fiscal year's actual dividend of 28.00 yen. The interim dividends for the second and third quarters, as well as the year-end dividend, have each been raised by 1.50 yen to 9.50 yen per share.

The revision was prompted by upward adjustments to the company's full-year earnings forecasts. Net profit attributable to parent company shareholders is now projected at 33.9 billion yen for the full year, an increase of 4.5 billion yen from the previous forecast. Operating profit is expected to reach 51.1 billion yen, up 6.7 billion yen. The company cited stronger-than-anticipated increases in net interest margin driven by increased average loan balances and the Bank of Japan's policy rate hikes as the primary factors supporting the earnings upgrade.

The expected payout ratio for the full year is approximately 40 percent. The company's dividend policy reflects confidence in sustaining improved profitability driven by its lending growth and the favorable interest rate environment.
